recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants more specific normative TLS/BCP195 requirements; the current source already covers the Jira's R5 subscriber-side security concerns without duplicating guidance elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-18993 asked the Subscription resource to more explicitly address subscriber-side security: using headers or secrets to let subscribers trust notifications, avoiding insecure handling of those values, limiting exposure of sensitive Subscription data such as endpoints, and warning subscribers about fake notifications that could trigger denial-of-service behavior.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied through dbeb5e6a7a, which moved Subscription safety guidance into source/subscriptions.html while mentioning FHIR#18993, and through 3a6fa70bed, explicitly titled "FHIR-18994, FHIR-18993, FHIR-19621 - Additional security considerations." The latter added HTTPS/rest-hook guidance, warnings about sensitive Subscription data including privileged endpoints, and fake-notification denial-of-service guidance. FHIR-39034 later renamed the header mechanism to Subscription.parameter without changing the security intent.
additional_context: FHIR-18994 is a Published companion issue whose resolution says to handle broader Subscription security considerations as part of FHIR-18993. FHIR-19621 is a Duplicate whose resolution says the rest-hook HTTPS warning will be addressed as part of FHIR-18993; its linked Zulip thread discusses REST-hook payload, endpoint trust, TLS/SNI validation, payload minimization, and authorization risk. Subscription, SubscriptionStatus, and SubscriptionTopic are active resources in source/fhir.ini, and the Subscription resource notes link Safety and Security to the Subscriptions Framework page.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/subscriptions.html already covers authorization at creation and notification time, payload minimization, HTTPS/rest-hook channel security, sensitive Subscription data and privileged endpoints, limited-use secrets via Subscription.parameter, validating incoming messages, and fake-notification denial-of-service defenses.
